how: Read the complete ray-semigroup argument, Cramer minor bound, independent-ray fundamental-parallelepiped reduction, same-degree Noether normalization, local-to-graded regular-sequence argument, and shifted constituent bound. Verified all hypotheses and exclusion of the constant algebra.

Read the complete canonical branching-algebra proof and source identifications, including multiplication, external grading at zero weights, determinant units removed by semisimple restriction, degree-L prime avoidance for every parameter prefix, and graded GL-to-SL isomorphism on centrally balanced rays.

Read the entire normalized-highest-weight finiteness proof, explicit Weyl-factor bounds n<=m and delta_i<=m-1, determinant-twist elimination, finite maximum, m=1 case and optimal-envelope equivalences with the ordinary GL_n scope.

Read the entire highest-weight algebra proof, compatible Cartan multiplication, explicit covariants and quadratic identity, independence via specialization, odd valuation injectivity, Hilbert-piece surjectivity, positive basis, integral flatness and finite-characteristic qualification.

Read the entire two-proof cubic argument; independently checked smoothness including endpoints, dual-coordinate convention, full regraded invariant ring and Cartan multiplication, torus recurrence, stabilizer determinant order, parameter-ideal nilpotence, and exponential versus h=O(n6). Opened the primary discriminant source and its exact statement. Scope restricted to canonical clause.

Read the entire universal-denominator and fixed-target covariant proof, including nonzero discriminant powers, the pole after regrading, exact-sequence alternative, and eventual-period divisibility. Independently checked the normal hypersurface and multivariate radial-cancellation examples. Directly read Derksen Theorem3.6 p594. This event covers the core and initial counterexamples; any later additions receive a separate check.

Read the complete toric proof: unique fundamental-parallelepiped decomposition and degree count, normality by halfspace intersections, finite free parameters, face quotient and lexicographic minimality. Directly checked Danilov Proposition8.5.1 pp124-125. Exact canonical degree D and positive Hilbert form verified.

Read the entire Markov recurrence proof, all divisibility hypotheses of CGLS Corollary1.5 p4, lattice count and translation, primitive rays, normality, canonical interior-ideal translation, rational singularities, two-dimensional face lower bound and exact lex-minimal tuple. Directly opened and read the CGLS and Danilov primary statements. No factoriality or ordinary-plethysm identification inferred.

Read the entire added SL2 x SL4 example. Rechecked maximal-minor realization and sole relation, exact Hilbert cancellation, quotient divisor, factorization through connected character-free group, and the quadric-cone resolution with higher cohomology vanishing. Counterexample is to exact factor transfer, not a quantitative separation.

Read the complete Koszul/trace proof, rederived the residue-class leading-term formula and its shifts, checked generic reducedness of the fixed scheme, regular local excess Koszul homology, natural equivariance and nonzero determinant ratio. Unique maximal component and generic ambient smoothness are retained as hypotheses.

Author whole-proof reread. Checked every tridiagonal rank case including n=4, full automorphism induction and ternary base case, determinant kernel, exact diagonal generator, 2-adic monomial classification, smooth quotient tangent sequence and irreducible fixed-component inference. Directly read Huybrechts Ch3 Cor1.6/Ex1.4 and Luna III.1 theorem and smooth-point remark; refined Luna locator to pp97-98.

Read full canonical binary-form regrading, known zero-table specialization, off-residue strict-saturation qualification, and explicit common-degree parameter envelope from bounded null-cone equations. No polynomial h.s.o.p. bound or strict saturation bound13 inferred.

Read the full added evaluation-ring argument on the 3-not-dividing-n subsequence: fixedness restricts surviving degrees to M multiples, and the discriminant of stretch degree M has nonzero evaluation, so the orbit-closure image is exactly C[u^M] and its regraded multiplicity is one.

Whole-proof reading: determinant-correct quotient lift, unique closed orbit, Jordan semisimple replacement, projection of the finitely generated eigenvalue group to two-primary torsion, smooth-coordinate doubling chain, complete equality case, and scheme-theoretic smooth fixed-locus classification. The nonsplit abstract extension is expressly not claimed to be a cubic example.

Read the complete proof. Independently checked rational-span necessity, all-ones torsion character, rank-deficient Cramer and maximal-minor bound, tree cofactors, two-term cycle determinant including double edges, extremal rooted-tree depth, chain spectrum and exclusion of all extra cubic monomials. The conclusion excludes only graph-support competitors and leaves three-distinct-variable supports open.

Read the entire proof: exact grading stabilizer via full linear stabilizer and unique closed orbit, numerical semigroup regrading and leading multiplicity one for all n>=4, cyclotomic uniformizer/product identity, moving cubic and adjoint weight enumeration, recurrence checks for both finite sums and conormal valuation. Verified explicit restriction to a local coefficient, with no global Laurent-coefficient or dominance assertion.

Read the complete connected-graph extension: full-rank graph subform forces the chain spectrum; in rank n-1 the signed cofactor vector is a common power of two times powers of -2, the nonzero three-term sum valuation is bounded, and the extremal tree minor has a unique maximum-height vertex. This excludes all connected graph parts, even with additional triple monomials.

Read the complete proof: include all independent cube columns in a support-span basis, apply Cramer to a nonzero maximal minor, expand odd cube factors, apply the proved column-norm determinant inequality, and use the extra factor three in the full-rank all-triple case. Both numerical bounds are strictly below 2^(n-1); deficient rank and arbitrary finite lift order are covered.
